q-110422.name: Question 1
q-110422.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}4xy, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

The marginal CDF ${F}_{X}(x)$ of $X$ is given by

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ g(x), & 0\le x\le 1 \\ 1 & x>1.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the function $g(x)?$
q-110422.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4xy\,\text{d}y \\  & =4x{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =2x[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =2x({1}^{2}-0) \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the marginal CDF of $X$ for $0\le x\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}{f}_{X}(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{x}2u\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[{u}^{2}]}_{0}^{x} \\  & ={x}^{2}-0 \\  & ={x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${F}_{X}(x)$ is

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ {x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1 \\ 1 & x>1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $g(x)={x}^{2}.$

q-142703.name: Question 2
q-142703.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=15{x}^{2}y,\,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{X}(x).$
q-142703.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 1\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14192927/assets/dfa15482cfa0e8fdc9e98b05a71d2b64a89b3886da44f6966fee9f1b5e096eef.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}15{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =15{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =15{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{15}{2}[{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{15}{2}[{x}^{2}\cdot {(\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}})}^{2}-{x}^{2}\cdot {0}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{15}{2}[{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})-0] \\  & =\frac{15({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{15({x}^{2}-{x}^{4})}{2}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142707.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with a joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{xy}{2},\,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4.
$$

Find the expression for the marginal PDF ${f}_{Y}(y).$
q-142707.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0,\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4\}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14192927/assets/f65ef4fc9d7ae895bc7ba8fe99bc7b03d8b26c92611fcbc43f600aa2e0c30301.png)

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $0\le y\le 2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\frac{xy}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}xy\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}y]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{x}^{2}y]_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{(\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}})}^{2}\cdot y-{0}^{2}\cdot y] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4-{y}^{2})y-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[4y-{y}^{3}] \\  & =y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{4}, & 0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142908.name: Question 4
q-142908.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{x}\,y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,2\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X<0.5).$
q-142908.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{3}{5}\sqrt{x}\,y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{x}\,{y}^{2}]}_{y=2}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{x}({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<0.5) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0.5}{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{0.5}(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{x})\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{0.5} \\  & =[{0.5}^{3/2}]-[{0}^{3/2}] \\  & ≈0.3536.\end{aligned}
$$

q-142909.name: Question 5
q-142909.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{19}x\sqrt{y}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,4\le y\le 9, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X\ge 1.9).$
q-142909.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $1\le x\le 2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{4}^{9}\frac{1}{19}x\sqrt{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{19}x{[\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3/2}]}_{y=4}^{y=9} \\  & =\frac{2}{57}x{[{y}^{3/2}]}_{y=4}^{y=9} \\  & =\frac{2}{57}x({9}^{3/2}-{4}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}x, & 1\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 1.9) & ={\int }_{1.9}^{\infty }{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1.9}^{2}\frac{2}{3}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{1.9}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[{2}^{2}-{1.9}^{2}] \\  & =0.13.\end{aligned}
$$
